elements.content: Communication Goal: I can introduce myself, say what I do, and ask others about their jobs.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 1. Hello there!
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Time to show off
- Materials: Dialogue cards, name badges, whiteboard, COSYmanuals 'to be' and 'question words' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• greet and introduce yourself
• talk about jobs with a/an
• ask and answer 'What do you do?'
Recycling & Course Continuity:

Prior learning: Recycles greetings and introductions from Lesson 1.

Next lesson: Lesson 3 recycles jobs to talk about daily routines.
Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

nice — pleasant or kind. Example: She is a nice person.
welcome — a friendly greeting to a guest. Example: Welcome to our home!
excuse — a polite word used to get attention or say sorry. Example: Excuse me, is this your book?
happy — feeling good and positive. Example: I am happy today.
student — a person who studies. Example: I am a student.
teacher — a person who helps students learn. Example: She is my English teacher.
friend — a person you like and know well. Example: Tom is my best friend.
fine — well or okay. Example: I am fine, thank you.
thank — to say you are grateful. Example: Thank you for your help.
goodbye — a word you say when you leave. Example: Goodbye, see you tomorrow.
designer — a person who designs things. Example: She is a UX designer.
engineer — a person who designs or builds machines and systems. Example: He is a software engineer.
nurse — a person who cares for sick people. Example: She is a nurse in a hospital.
chef — a person who cooks in a restaurant. Example: He is a chef in a small bistro.
manager — a person who leads a team. Example: She is a project manager.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Nice to meet you. (polite introduction)
• What do you do? (asking about a job)
• I'm a designer. (stating a job with a/an)
• I'm an engineer. (stating a job with a/an)
• Are you a student? — No, I'm a freelancer. (asking and answering about work)
• I work in an office. / I work from home. (talking about a workplace)
• Excuse me, can you repeat that? (polite survival phrase)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'pleasant or kind'?
Which word means 'a friendly greeting to a guest'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Pronunciation Focus: Polite intonation and the /w/ sound in 'welcome'

welcome /ˈwelkəm/ — stress the first syllable
excuse /ɪkˈskjuːz/ — stress the second syllable
thank /θæŋk/ — voiceless th
goodbye /ɡʊdˈbaɪ/ — stress the second syllable
Listen and repeat:
Nice to meet you. Welcome to our class. How are you? I'm fine, thanks.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'a/an' for one non-specific countable noun and 'the' for a specific noun.

Form:
Articles: a / an / the: a + consonant sound (a teacher), an + vowel sound (an engineer), the + specific noun (the teacher in our class).

Examples:
• She is a teacher.
• He is an engineer.
• The teacher is in the classroom.
• I have a book and an apple.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My mother is ___ nurse.
He is ___ engineer.
___ doctor in our town is very kind.
I have ___ apple and ___ banana.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• She is a ... (teacher / doctor / manager).
• He is an ... (engineer / actor / artist).
• The ... is ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is your job or dream job?
• Who is a hero in your community?
• Where does a nurse work?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about jobs with 'a' and 'an'.
• Write three sentences about people in your community with 'the'.
Reading: Time to show off

Hello! My name is David. I am a new student. This is my friend Sara. She is a teacher. She works in a school. My brother is an engineer. He works for a big company. My sister is a nurse. She works in a hospital. What do you do? Are you a student? Excuse me, can you repeat that? Yes, of course. Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
What is Sara's job?
Where does David's brother work?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: Good morning! Welcome to our class.
B: Good morning. Nice to meet you.
A: Nice to meet you too. What do you do?
B: I'm a designer. I work from home. And you?
A: I'm a teacher. I work in a school.
B: Excuse me, can you repeat that?
A: Yes, I'm a teacher. I work in a school.
What does the first speaker do?
Where does the teacher work?
Speaking task: Ask three classmates what they do and where they work. Report one answer to the group.

• What do you do?
• Where do you work or study?
• Do you work from home or in an office?
• What job do you want?
• Which job helps people most?
Role-play: You are at a networking event. Introduce yourself, say what you do, and ask three people about their jobs.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about you and your family's jobs.
Model: I'm a ... My mother is a ... My father is an ... She works in ... He works for ...
